meta.title: Digimon World: Horizon
meta.description: A new story, Digimon from three other games, 60 fps and a new translation for Digimon World on the PlayStation. Patch your own discs in the browser.
lang.label: Language
hero.title: The Digimon World you remember, and a lot more.
patcher.title: Patch your disc
patcher.lead: To make the final Horizon disc you need to load your discs of Digimon World, Digimon Digital Card Battle, Digimon World 2 and Digimon World 3 / 2003. Your disc is made from them. Any language and any common format works: we support them all.
patcher.dropHint: Drop your discs to add them
patch.needSources: Add the three source game discs. Their models are converted here on your computer.
patch.ready: Ready. It takes a few minutes, here in your browser.
features.title: What's new
features.lead: Choose language, font, difficulty, new Digimon, extended story and display settings in OPTIONS. Engine and bug fixes always apply.
changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.lead: What each release brings to your game.
privacy.title: Everything is local, in your browser
privacy.body: Your discs are patched right here, in your browser. They never go out to the internet and nothing is uploaded. You do not download the final image from any server either: it is made on your computer from your own discs.
privacy.audit: You can audit all of it:
desktop.title: Prefer an app?
desktop.lead: Horizon Patcher is this same patcher as a program for Windows and macOS. It runs on your computer and uploads nothing; it downloads the release from GitHub only when you ask it to.
desktop.phone: It is for computers: open this page on your Windows PC or Mac to download it.
desktop.linux: On Linux, use the builder above in your browser, or {link} from the command line.
desktop.win1: Unzip it first: right-click the zip and choose **Extract All**. Keep the Horizon Patcher folder together and open **Horizon Patcher.exe** in it.
desktop.win2: If Windows says **Windows protected your PC**, click **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
desktop.win3: If Windows blocks the files, right-click the zip, choose **Properties**, tick **Unblock**, click **OK** and unzip it again.
desktop.mac1: Double-click the zip to unzip it, then double-click **Horizon Patcher**.
desktop.mac2: If macOS says it cannot be opened (Apple cannot check it, or it is from an unidentified developer): open **System Settings › Privacy & Security**, scroll down, click **Open Anyway** next to Horizon Patcher and confirm.
desktop.mac3: On macOS 14 or earlier you can instead right-click (or Control-click) the app, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
desktop.macNotarized: It is notarized by Apple, so macOS opens it without asking.
desktop.macMore: Does macOS say the app is damaged? See {link}.
desktop.safe: Both apps are built by GitHub Actions from the public source code of {tag}, with nothing added by hand:
desktop.unsigned: They are not signed yet with a certificate your system knows, which is why it asks you the first time.
desktop.check: To check your download, its SHA-256 must be:

why.badDump: It looks like {game}, but it is not the original dump: a modified, damaged or differently ripped image (its checksum does not match).

why.encrypted: The archive has a password. Unpack it yourself and add the .bin/.cue.

why.archiveBroken: This archive cannot be opened. It may be damaged or not fully downloaded.

why.ecmChecksum: The ECM file is damaged: its checksum does not match.

why.notImage: This is not a disc image. Add the .bin (or the .bin and .cue together).

why.chd: CHD files cannot be opened in the browser yet. Convert it to .bin/.cue with chdman: chdman extractcd -i game.chd -o game.cue

data.noScript: All data is available below. Search and sorting need JavaScript.
data.learningRule: Enemy execution of a normal technique records it for learning; it need not land a hit. At battle end, your partner must not already know it, must have it in its species list, and must have a matching specialty. The first matching slot selects the chance below.
data.brainsRule: Brains does not affect this battle roll.
data.oneRule: If several techniques pass their rolls, one is learned at random. Repeated casts do not add extra rolls for the same technique.
data.costRule: Chances are per candidate roll, not a guaranteed final award. MP is the base battle cost (data cost ×3), before condition and Brains modifiers. Finishers cost no MP. Status percentages apply on a successful hit. Finishers and intrinsic moves have no battle learning chance. Shared names show their data IDs.
data.speciesRule: All partner-enabled forms, including special and laboratory forms. Specialties keep their original slot positions. Expand a move list for its effective battle roll. A listed move without a matching specialty cannot be learned in battle by that form. Finisher power includes species-specific overrides.
data.routeRule3: Read a target’s row for its requirements. Ordinary evolution needs
data.routeRule5: : care mistakes, weight, stats, and bonus. All listed stats must meet their thresholds, except Rookie targets, which test the highest stat instead (ties: Brains, Speed, Defense, Offense, MP, HP). Any one listed bonus condition earns the bonus point. Happiness uses the status screen’s 0–100 scale; wins and care mistakes count in the current form.
data.pickerRule: Selection favors a target you have not raised yet. For Rookie→Champion and Champion→Ultimate candidates scoring 3, it then compares the average of required stats (HP/MP divided by 10). The documented picker carries its average accumulator after a qualifying loser, so list order can affect this comparison. In-Training→Rookie keeps the best score and the first listed target on a tie. Fresh growth is fixed. Special and timed routes have their own triggers; item routes are outside this table.
data.recruit.title: Recruits
data.recruit.intro: Every City recruit in the extended story. Times use the game clock; hour endpoints include the whole hour. Battle HP includes map adjustments. Story choices can change the route, but do not permanently block a recruit. Spoilers ahead.
